tokyo_giaggiolo_ginza.gf_detail: Ask. An Italian restaurant known for its organic vegetable "15-herb salad" and gentle, broth-led cooking (a maternity course is offered); no source describes the pasta or bread situation or a gluten-free option.
tokyo_giaggiolo_ginza.vegan_detail: Ask. The signature herb and organic vegetable salad may suit, but its dressing and toppings are not described, and courses include prosciutto.
tokyo_giaggiolo_ginza.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 11:30–14:30 (food L.O. 13:00) and 17:30–21:30 (food L.O. 19:30); closed Sundays and Mondays (Tabelog). Cards accepted.
tokyo_giaggiolo_ginza.notes: [Italian · the 15-herb salad] A long-established, softly lit basement Italian restaurant in Ginza 7-chōme, open since July 2007. The signature is the '15 Herb Salad' of organic vegetables and herbs, which a regular says is inspired by the old Florentine pharmacy Santa Maria Novella. It comes in a large size with all the toppings, and can be taken away. The cooking is gentle and led by ingredients and broth, with a maternity course for pregnant guests and non-alcoholic sparkling and wine. Dinner courses open with herb salad and prosciutto. About ¥10,000–15,000 a head at dinner.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or chef.

anecdotes.text: "I always have to order the signature '15 Herb Salad.' This dish, inspired by the world's oldest pharmacy, Santa Maria Novella, truly revitalizes me." — May 2026.
"I made a reservation for a maternity course to celebrate a special occasion! The menu was gentle on the body of a pregnant woman." — September 2026.

tokyo_matri_kitchen_higashi_ginza.gf_detail: Not gluten-free as described: Russian dishes such as pelmeni (wheat dumplings) and beef stroganoff with borscht and bread; no gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_matri_kitchen_higashi_ginza.vegan_detail: Not vegan as described: meat pelmeni, beef stroganoff; borscht's stock is not described.
tokyo_matri_kitchen_higashi_ginza.hours_raw: Mon–Wed and Fri–Sun 11:30–22:00; closed Thursdays (Tabelog). Cards, IC and d Barai accepted.
tokyo_matri_kitchen_higashi_ginza.notes: [Russian · a busy ¥1,300 lunch] A 20-seat Russian restaurant on a Higashi-Ginza second floor, with cheerful staff who reviewers say seem to be Russian. The weekday lunch set is ¥1,300 with a drink: a main such as beef stroganoff, plus salad and borscht. Add pelmeni, which appear to be made fresh before boiling, so they take a while at busy times. Russian tea comes with jam. Queues form before the 11:30 opening. Dinner runs to 22:00, about ¥2,000–3,000 a head.

chef_bio.origin: Higashi-Ginza; opening date not found in a source read

anecdotes.text: "I thought they would just boil frozen ones, but it seems they probably make them fresh before boiling? It took quite a while, but they were delicious." — September 2026.
"I ordered the lunch set, which featured stroganoff as the main dish, along with a salad, borscht, and a drink, all for a very reasonable price of JPY 1,300." — October 2026.

tokyo_gramercy_table_ginza5.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: a bistro whose lunch favourite is truffle omurice with salad and bread, plus hamburgers; no gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_gramercy_table_ginza5.vegan_detail: Not vegan as described: omurice (egg), hamburgers and bistro mains.
tokyo_gramercy_table_ginza5.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:30–14:00 and 18:00–21:00; closed Sundays (Tabelog). Dinner: 10% service and ¥540 charge. Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners) accepted.
tokyo_gramercy_table_ginza5.notes: [Bistro · truffle omurice down an alley] A 20-seat bistro a short way down an alley off Ginza's main streets, open since October 2012. A June 2026 diner likens its black decor, large windows, open kitchen and lit plants to a New York townhouse restaurant. The lunch favourite is truffle omurice with salad and bread, limited to five servings on Saturdays. The menu has since added hamburgers. Regulars note staff remember them after years. Dinner is a fuller evening, about ¥30,000–40,000 in one June 2026 review. Lunch runs about ¥1,000–5,000. A 10% service charge and ¥540 charge apply at dinner.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or chef.

anecdotes.text: "I visited after several years, and I was delighted that the staff remembered me… I went with my favorite, the truffle omurice." — September 2026.
"My companion wanted to try the limited 5 servings of Omurice, so we arrived before opening." — June 2026, a Saturday.
